exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.summary: Strengthens the buttocks and the back of the thighs while keeping the lower back supported.
steps: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
Rest your arms by your sides, palms down. Gently tighten your stomach muscles.
Squeeze your buttocks and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Hold at the top for 3 seconds, breathing normally.
Slowly lower your hips back to the floor, one vertebra at a time.
do: Push evenly through both heels.
Keep your knees pointing straight ahead, in line with your hips.
Move slowly and with control, especially on the way down.
avoid: Arching your lower back at the top of the lift.
Holding your breath.
Letting your knees fall in toward each other.

exercises.name: Clamshell
exercises.summary: Targets the side hip muscles that help keep the pelvis and knee stable when walking.
steps: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent to about 45 degrees and your heels in line with your buttocks.
Rest your head on your lower arm or a pillow. Place your top hand on your top hip.
Keeping your feet together, lift your top knee as far as you can without rolling your pelvis backward.
Hold for 2 seconds at the top.
Slowly lower your knee back down. Repeat, then switch sides.
do: Keep your hips stacked one on top of the other.
Keep your feet touching throughout the movement.
Feel the work in the side of your hip, not your lower back.
avoid: Rolling your top hip backward to lift the knee higher.
Rushing through repetitions.
Lifting your feet apart.

exercises.name: Seated Knee Extension
exercises.summary: Strengthens the muscles at the front of the thigh (quadriceps) that straighten and support the knee.
steps: Sit tall in a sturdy chair with your back supported and both feet flat on the floor.
Hold the sides of the seat lightly for balance.
Slowly straighten one knee, lifting your foot until your leg is as straight as is comfortable.
Tighten the muscle on the top of your thigh and hold for 5 seconds.
Slowly lower your foot back to the floor. Complete all repetitions, then switch legs.
do: Point your toes toward the ceiling at the top.
Keep your thigh resting on the chair.
Sit upright with your shoulders relaxed.
avoid: Swinging or kicking your leg up quickly.
Leaning back in the chair to lift higher.
Locking your knee forcefully at the top.

exercises.name: Heel Slide
exercises.summary: Gently restores knee and hip bending range, often used early in knee rehabilitation.
steps: Lie on your back on a firm surface with both legs straight.
Rest your arms by your sides and relax your shoulders.
Slowly slide the heel of one leg toward your buttocks, bending the knee as far as is comfortable.
Hold for 2 seconds at the end of the movement.
Slowly slide the heel back down until the leg is straight again. Complete all repetitions, then switch legs.
do: Keep your heel in contact with the surface the whole time.
Move slowly and smoothly.
Wear a sock or place a towel under your heel so it glides easily.
avoid: Lifting your foot off the surface.
Forcing the knee into a painful bend.
Letting the knee drop out to the side.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.summary: Strengthens the calf muscles and supports ankle stability and balance.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, close to a counter or sturdy chair you can hold for balance.
Keep your knees straight but not locked.
Slowly rise up onto the balls of both feet, lifting your heels as high as you comfortably can.
Hold at the top for 1 second.
Slowly lower your heels back to the floor.
do: Keep your weight centred over your big and second toes.
Lower more slowly than you rise.
Hold a support lightly if your balance is unsteady.
avoid: Letting your ankles roll outward.
Bouncing or rushing the movement.
Leaning forward at the hips.

exercises.name: Chin Tuck
exercises.summary: Strengthens the deep neck muscles and encourages good head and neck posture.
steps: Sit tall in a chair with your feet flat and your hands resting on your thighs.
Look straight ahead, keeping your eyes level.
Gently glide your head straight back, as if making a double chin.
Hold for 5 seconds. You should feel a gentle stretch at the base of your skull.
Relax back to the starting position.
do: Keep your eyes level, as if your head is sliding on a shelf.
Keep the movement small and gentle.
Breathe normally throughout.
avoid: Tipping your head up or nodding down.
Pushing into pain or dizziness.
Shrugging your shoulders.

exercises.name: Standing Shoulder Flexion
exercises.summary: Maintains and improves the shoulder's ability to raise the arm overhead.
steps: Stand tall with your arms relaxed at your sides, thumbs pointing forward.
Gently tighten your stomach muscles to keep your back steady.
Keeping your elbows straight, slowly raise both arms forward and up as high as is comfortable.
Hold for 2 seconds at the top.
Slowly lower your arms back to your sides.
do: Raise your arms only as high as is comfortable.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Move smoothly in both directions.
avoid: Arching your lower back to get your arms higher.
Shrugging your shoulders.
Swinging your arms with momentum.

exercises.name: Prone Hip Extension
exercises.summary: Strengthens the buttock muscles that extend the hip, with the trunk supported by the floor.
steps: Lie face down on a mat with your legs straight. Rest your forehead on your folded hands.
Gently tighten your stomach and buttock muscles.
Keeping your knee straight, slowly raise one leg a few inches off the floor.
Lift only as high as you can without your lower back arching.
Slowly lower the leg back down. Complete the set, then switch legs.
do: Keep your knee straight and your toes pointing toward the floor.
Keep both hips pressed into the mat.
Move slowly and with control.
avoid: Arching or twisting your lower back to lift higher.
Bending the knee.
Holding your breath.

exercises.name: Prone Press-Up on Elbows
exercises.summary: Gently moves the lower back into extension by propping the upper body up on the forearms.
steps: Lie face down with your forearms on the floor and your elbows close to your sides.
Relax your buttocks, legs and lower back.
Slowly push through your forearms to lift your chest, bringing your elbows under your shoulders.
Pause briefly in the propped position, letting your lower back sag and relax.
Slowly lower back down to the floor.
do: Keep your hips and pelvis relaxed on the floor.
Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Breathe out as you rise.
avoid: Tensing your buttocks or lifting your hips.
Pushing into sharp or spreading pain.
Craning your neck upward.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.summary: A restful stretch for the lower back and hips.
steps: Kneel on a padded surface, with your knees wide and your big toes touching. A folded blanket under the knees helps.
If the knees feel tight, place a second folded blanket between your calves and thighs.
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Fold forward and rest your forehead on the floor, reaching your arms forward along the mat.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20–30 seconds, then walk your hands back to sit up.
do: Let your back round gently and relax.
Use a block or pillow under your forehead if it doesn't reach the floor.
Breathe deeply into your back.
avoid: Forcing your hips down onto your heels.
Holding a position that causes knee pain.
Holding your breath.

exercises.name: Child's Pose Side Bend
exercises.summary: Adds a side stretch to child's pose, lengthening the muscles along the side of the trunk.
steps: Kneel with your knees wider than your hips and your big toes touching.
Fold forward into child's pose, with your arms reaching forward and your forehead on the floor.
Take a breath, then walk both hands over to one side as far as is comfortable.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, feeling the stretch along the opposite side of your trunk.
Walk your hands back to the centre, then repeat to the other side.
do: Keep your hips sitting back toward your heels.
Move your hands in small steps.
Breathe into the side that is stretching.
avoid: Letting your hips lift or slide sideways.
Bouncing into the stretch.
Pushing into pain.

exercises.name: Supine Piriformis Stretch
exercises.summary: Stretches the deep buttock muscles (piriformis) with the other foot resting on the floor.
steps: Lie on your back with both knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Cross one leg over so its ankle rests on the opposite knee.
Hold the crossed leg just below its knee.
Gently draw that knee toward your opposite shoulder until you feel a stretch in the buttock.
Hold for 20–30 seconds, relax, then switch sides.
do: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Pull gently and steadily.
Keep your lower back resting on the floor.
avoid: Pulling hard enough to cause pain in the knee or hip.
Lifting your head or shoulders.
Bouncing.

exercises.name: Cervical Extension
exercises.summary: Active range of motion for the neck, bending backward after first setting a chin tuck.
steps: Sit upright in a chair. If your clinician gave you a strap or towel, hold its ends with it looped around the base of your neck.
Gently tuck your chin straight back.
Slowly tip your head back to look up, as far as is comfortable.
Bring your head back up to the starting position.
Repeat slowly.
do: Move your head straight back and forth, with no turning to either side.
Move slowly through a comfortable range.
Keep your shoulders relaxed.
avoid: Rotating or tilting your head to one side.
Moving into dizziness, tingling or pain.
Jerking the movement.

exercises.name: Seated Thoracic Lumbar Extension
exercises.summary: Gently arches the upper and lower back to improve extension mobility.
steps: Sit upright toward the front of a sturdy chair with your feet flat.
Cross your arms over your chest, with your hands resting on your shoulders.
Slowly arch your trunk backward, lifting your chest toward the ceiling.
Hold briefly at the end of the movement.
Return to upright and repeat.
do: Move slowly and with control.
Lead with your chest.
Keep your feet planted.
avoid: Moving into pain.
Throwing your head back.
Leaning so far that you lose balance.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Open Book
exercises.summary: A rotation stretch for the upper back and chest, keeping the hips still.
steps: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent and your knees together. A pillow under your head helps.
Stretch both arms straight out in front of you on the floor, palms together.
Slide your top hand forward and back over the bottom hand a few times to loosen up.
Then lift your top arm up and over, rotating your upper back to reach toward the floor behind you.
Pause, then bring the arm back to the starting position.
do: Keep your knees together and your hips facing forward.
Let your eyes and head follow your moving hand.
Breathe out as you open.
avoid: Letting your knees or hips roll backward.
Forcing the arm to the floor.
Moving into shoulder pain.
